MA No. 1174/2015 has been filed by the owner and driver of the vehicle under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, being aggrieved by the Award dated 21.08.2015 passed by the Member,
Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, District Bhind (M.P.) (hereinafter referred to as "the Claims Tribunal") in Claim Case No. 39/2014.

Similarly, MA No. 636/2015 has been filed by the owner and driver under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, being aggrieved by the Award dated 01.04.2016 passed by the Second Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, District Bhind (M.P.)
in Claim Case No. 17/2016, whereby the Claims Tribunal, by exonerating the Insurance Company,
imposed liability upon the owner and driver to pay compensation in favor of the claimants.

sentences.text:
2. The date of the accident and the issue of negligence are not in dispute; however, the dispute pertains only to the liability.
3.

Shri R.P. Gupta, learned counsel appearing for the owner and driver of the vehicle, submits that at the time of the accident, the driver of the offending vehicle was holding a valid and effective driving licence for a light motor vehicle (LMV).
Since the vehicle weighs less than 7,500 kilograms, a light commercial vehicle endorsement is not required.
Section 10 of Motor Vehicles Act defines a licence to drive a light motor vehicle but does not define a licence to drive a light commercial vehicle.
The Claims Tribunal has committed an error in holding that there was a breach of terms and NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:4687 3 MA-1174-2015 conditions of insurance policy.
4. On the other hand, learned counsel for Insurance Company opposed the prayer and prayed for dismissal of the appeals.

5. Heard the arguments advanced by learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
6.

It is not disputed that at the time of the accident, the driver of the offending vehicle, i.e., Bolero MP 06-GA 1788, was holding a licence to drive a light motor vehicle and the claimant was a third party.
It is also not disputed that at the time of the accident, the driver was driving the offending vehicle, and the weight of the offending vehicle was less than 7,500 kgs.

In this regard, reliance can be placed upon the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Mukund Dewangan vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. , AIR 2017 SC 3668, wherein the Apex Court held that:-
''...in the case of a light motor vehicle (LMV), a person holding a valid LMV driving licence is competent to drive a light commercial vehicle (LCV) if the weight of the Indrabhansingh vs Smt. Priti on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/16963816/
2 vehicle does not exceed 7,500 kgs.

entities.text: Mukund Dewangan vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. , AIR 2017 SC 3668
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, there is no breach of terms of the insurance policy in the present case."

7. In light of the aforementioned judgment, it is clear that the driver of the offending vehicle,
holding a valid driving licence for a light motor vehicle, was competent to drive the vehicle, which weighs less than 7,500 kgs.
The absence of a separate endorsement for light commercial vehicles does not amount to a violation of the terms and conditions of the insurance policy.
Therefore, there is no need for a separate endorsement.

The Claims Tribunal has committed an error by exonerating the Insurance Company on this point only and the Insurance Company is liable to pay the compensation amount despite the absence of a specific endorsement for plying the vehicle.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:4687 4 MA-1174-2015 8.
Accordingly, the misc. appeals filed by the owner and driver of the offending vehicle deserve to be and are hereby allowed and disposed of to the extent indicated above.
